subject: Electrical Engineering
title: The Lorentz Force in a Motor
description: A quick, practical guide to The Lorentz Force in a Motor.

hook.text: Send current through a wire in a magnetic field and the wire moves. Every motor exploits this.

buildup.text: F = IL × B. Current, wire length, and field strength multiply to give force.

discovery.text: The force is perpendicular to both the current and the field. Use the right-hand rule.

twist.text: Reverse the current and the force reverses. That's how motors switch direction.

climax.text: Every coil in every motor feels this force — scaled up millions of times.

punchline.text: Current in a field makes force — the one law behind every motor.

quiz.question: How does a motor reverse direction?
options: By increasing the magnetic field strength
By reversing the direction of the current
